title: Clean Coders Hate What Happens to Your Code When You Use These Enterprise Programming Tricks
summary: Kevlin Henney tours enterprise coding habits (trivial dependencies, cargo-cult conventions, noisy comments, factory overuse, verbose names, logging everything) and closes by refactoring a function down to its essence.

assertions.quote: one developer just broke node bab and thousands of projects and 11 lines of JavaScript

verdicts.note: The left-pad incident and subsequent supply-chain research show deep transitive dependency trees in npm expose projects to removals and malicious updates.

assertions.quote: this is how coding guidelines and Enterprise cultures are created by the repetition of an idea

verdicts.note: A sociological framing about how practices propagate.

assertions.quote: a misleading comment can be very confusing third the issue of typography comments clutter code

verdicts.note: Studies find comment-code inconsistency common after change, but comprehension research also shows explanatory comments help readers, so the claim holds for restating comments not all comments.

assertions.quote: if you tell people this is going to be six months worth of work they will pack it full to the six months and Beyond

verdicts.note: Parkinson's law and Brooks's law have anecdotal and some experimental support for deadline effects, but the ten-versus-hundred example is a single anecdote.

Software teams allowed to plan with their original (higher) estimates were less productive than those cut by up to 20%, and a company rewarding accurate estimates saw padded estimates with the buffer absorbed into extra work ('work stretching'); headcount is not addressed.
Review notes a self-fulfilling-prophecy effect: projects that over-estimate most likely effort can reach high accuracy by spending the remaining effort gold-plating the product.

assertions.quote: and this has led to as it were the over adoption of factory

verdicts.note: Prechelt's controlled pattern experiments found patterns help only when their flexibility is needed and otherwise add comprehension cost.

assertions.quote: the name is not merely a label on your design your name is your design

verdicts.note: Identifier studies show descriptive names improve comprehension; the specific heuristic about vague suffixes is expert opinion.

All five interviewed developers named identifier quality as a factor in understandability (generic names like processChar were called ambiguous), but none of the quantitative identifier metrics across 444 evaluations correlated more than weakly with understanding; nothing on 'Manager'-style names signalling weak design.

assertions.quote: logging is the most important single most important activity in that code base

verdicts.note: Anecdotal from client codebases; no measurement of logging proportion across projects.
